source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11 by the script programs/recipe63.sh, which wrote programs/RECIPE.log, from the table's own CA(66;4,38,2) (Paley matrix for q = 37 doubled, rows deleted; submission smolen-2026-11-debate11; programs/CA_66_4_38_2.txt). Columns 19, 32, 9 and 16 are dropped (the choice that leaves the three lightest rows with the fewest patterns only they cover). Then rows are removed one at a time, each time the row that is the only cover of the fewest patterns, and the array is repaired by simulated annealing in which every cell may change, with exact counts on all 4-sets and a move that writes a missing pattern into the closest of a few random rows (programs/fa_det.c). Every run has a fixed seed and stops on a count of moves. 65 rows after 4467 moves, 64 rows after 547705 moves, then rounds of three runs of at most 55000000 moves at temperatures 0.60, 0.55 and 0.65, each round continued from the output with the fewest missing patterns; rounds 0 to 4 ended with 4 missing, rounds 5 to 7 with 3, and round 8 reached 0 (command fa_det r7_1.txt 4 0.60 1 901 r8_1.txt -A -m 4 -I 55000000, 32055360 moves). A second run of the script from nothing gave the identical array (programs/REPLAY.log, programs/REPLAY.md). Exact check with ca_verify, all 4-sets
construction: Doubled Paley array for q = 37 with rows deleted, cut to 34 columns, three more rows removed one at a time with repair by simulated annealing on all cells
notes: ties the cited size 63 at k = 34; replaces the array of smolen-2026-11-t4-63at34 with a fully replayable one; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start
